item.title: New Unemployment Claims Fall to 189,000, Matching the Lowest Level Since 1969. Louisiana’s Are Down 29% From Last Year
item.description: Fewer Americans filed for unemployment last week than in almost any week since 1969. In Louisiana, about 1,150 people a week are filing, down from more than 1,600 a year ago.

item.title: Louisiana Wants America’s New Space Academy, and Starbase Louisiana Is Part of the Pitch
item.description: The state has asked NASA to put the U.S. Space Academy at LSU’s New Orleans campus, with 300 cadets in 2028 and 4,000 or more in time. No winner has been named.

item.title: Gas Is Dropping Fast for Thanksgiving: Gulf Coast Average Falls to $3.13, Down 51 Cents in Three Weeks
item.description: It is still about 48 cents higher than last Thanksgiving week. Diesel is the bigger story: $5.29 a gallon here, $1.84 more than a year ago.

item.title: Quarterfinal Friday: Kaplan Hosts Green Oaks, Delcambre Goes to No. 1 East Feliciana, Both at 7
item.description: The LHSAA has now posted both games. It will be dry and cold, with temperatures dropping toward the low 40s. Two wins from here is the Superdome.

item.title: Pecan Island and Downtown Abbeville Named Federal Opportunity Zones, Opening Tax Breaks for Investors
item.description: Two Vermilion Parish areas made the state’s new list. One covers the whole coast, including Pecan Island, where SpaceX plans to build. The breaks start Jan. 1.

item.title: Jensen Huang Gets His Job Back: Nvidia’s Board Reinstates Its CEO 11 Days After He Resigned
item.description: The board says it heard from “senior levels” of the U.S. government and is confident his return is no national security risk. An investigation into a foreign intelligence effort aimed at him is still open.

item.title: Louisiana Is Putting Up Billboards in Houston: ‘It’s Time to Come Home’
item.description: The state is going after Louisiana natives working in Texas, and Texas companies too. It says nearly 60,000 new jobs have been announced here since 2024.

item.title: Who’s Hiring Near Vermilion Parish This Week: Welders, a Dump Truck Driver in Abbeville, Mechanics and More
item.description: Ten trade jobs within driving distance, pulled from the state’s official job site. Two list pay. One is in Abbeville.

item.title: SpaceX Is Taking Resumes for Starbase Louisiana Now. Here’s the Email, and How Local Businesses Sign Up for the Work
item.description: The company says it will hire “heavily from nearby communities.” Its Louisiana page has a resume button, and there are two free sign-ups for contractors and suppliers.

item.title: New Order Tells Every Federal Contractor to Alert the White House Before Answering Congress
item.description: Companies that work for the federal government, and their subcontractors, must report requests from Congress and follow White House instructions on what to hold back. Breaking the rule could cost a company its contracts.

item.title: Louisiana Is Adding Construction Jobs Faster Than Any Other State: 17,600 in One Year
item.description: Federal numbers for October show construction work here up 13% from a year ago. No other state is close. The Lafayette area, which includes Vermilion Parish, added about 1,400.

item.title: Every SpaceX Job Open at Pecan Island Right Now: What Each One Requires and How to Apply
item.description: Eleven jobs as of Nov. 24. One needs only a high school diploma. Four start in Texas and move here in early 2027. None lists pay, and no welder, electrician, operator or laborer jobs are posted yet.

item.title: Trump Signs Law Ending the Penny and Letting Stores Round Cash Totals to the Nearest Nickel
item.description: Your pennies are still good money. But when a store can’t make exact change, the new law says how it may round. Cards and checks are not affected.

item.title: Ochsner Says Hackers Got Into Two Employee Accounts and Downloaded Files That May Include Social Security Numbers and Health Information
item.description: The hospital system, which runs Ochsner Abrom Kaplan Memorial Hospital in Kaplan, began notifying people Thursday. It says patient care and its medical records system were not disrupted, and it is still working out whose information was taken.

item.title: Kaplan Rolls 56-6 and Delcambre Wins Again: Both Parish Teams Reach the Quarterfinals
item.description: Kaplan routed Vidalia at home. Delcambre, the No. 25 seed, beat No. 9 Grand Lake 41-15 and now draws the top seed in its bracket.

item.title: SpaceX Starts Hiring Security for Pecan Island
item.description: Two listings went up this week, one to install cameras and access systems and one for executive protection. Neither requires a college degree. SpaceX now lists 12 jobs at Pecan Island.

item.title: Trump, Xi and Putin Sign a Four-Point Declaration: Nuclear Talks, More Fuel, U.N. Changes and a Warning to the International Criminal Court
item.description: The White House published the text from Thursday’s three-way summit in Shenzhen, China. It is short on specifics and sets no deadlines.

item.title: We Asked Vermilion Parish’s Three Power Providers How They Guard the Grid From Cyberattacks. One Answered.
item.description: Entergy sent a short statement. The City of Abbeville said it couldn’t verify an answer in time. SLEMCO did not respond.

item.title: Biscuit Sandwiches and Gravy Meals Sold From Break-Room Coolers in Louisiana Recalled Over Listeria Risk
item.description: The products went out through workplace break rooms, grab-and-go coolers and vending machines in Louisiana and six other states. No illnesses have been reported, the company says.

item.title: State Puts SpaceX’s Wharf and Road Permit Out for Public Comment. Here’s How to Weigh In.
item.description: Louisiana’s coastal permit office marked the application complete this week and sent it out for review. The 25-day comment window opens with a legal notice set to run Saturday.

item.title: White House: The FAA, Bank and Tech Outages Are Not Linked and Not a Cyberattack
item.description: The nation’s intelligence chief and Secretary of State Marco Rubio say the string of failures comes from companies and agencies patching and upgrading old systems.

item.title: Louisiana Will Need Nearly 42,000 Construction Workers by 2028, and the Lafayette Region Is Far Short, Report Says
item.description: A business group counted the workers needed to build 12 megaprojects, including SpaceX’s Starbase Louisiana in Vermilion Parish. It says three regions, Lafayette among them, could come up about 19,000 workers short.

item.title: Dry and in the 70s Through the Weekend, With Clear Skies for Playoff Friday
item.description: The National Weather Service forecast for Kaplan shows almost no chance of rain through Sunday. Kickoff temperatures Friday night should be in the 60s.

item.title: Democrat Mary Peltola Unseats Alaska Sen. Dan Sullivan, State’s Count Shows
item.description: With every precinct reporting, Alaska’s official tally gives Peltola just over 50% of first-choice votes, enough to win without a ranked-choice runoff count.

item.title: State Will Pay for Starlink Dishes at About 10,500 Louisiana Homes, Including a Couple Hundred in Vermilion Parish
item.description: Louisiana signed a broadband grant agreement with SpaceX’s Starlink in June. The state’s broadband chief says residents won’t pay for the equipment, and a new round of grants is opening now.

item.title: Playoff Friday: Kaplan Hosts Vidalia, Delcambre Goes to Grand Lake
item.description: Two Vermilion Parish teams are still alive in the LHSAA football playoffs. Both play in the regional round Friday night.

item.title: We Asked if South Louisiana’s FAA Sites Have the Router Behind the Ground Stop. The FAA Hasn’t Answered.
item.description: The agency’s press office did not reply by our Tuesday deadline. Its contractor, L3Harris, sent a statement that doesn’t mention Louisiana. Here is what is on the record and what isn’t.

item.title: Police Jury Wednesday: 2027 Budget Vote, a Response to the SpaceX Tax Deal Lawsuit and an Emergency Fix for the Mosquito Plane
item.description: Jurors meet at 5:30 p.m. at the courthouse, first to adopt next year’s budget and then for their regular monthly meeting. The agenda was posted Tuesday afternoon.

item.title: Sheriff’s Office: Langlinais Has Not Said RV Parks Are Banned, and He ‘Is Not Opposed’ to Them
item.description: Answering questions from the Times, the Sheriff’s Office also said it has no say over RV park permits. Those calls belong to local governing bodies, and Abbeville’s council takes up new RV parks tonight.

item.title: Apple Outage Hits the App Store, Apple Music and iCloud Sign-In, and Knocks Out App Store Connect for Every Developer
item.description: Apple’s own status pages show trouble starting about 10:45 a.m. Central Tuesday. Apple says an internal update caused it and that it wasn’t a cyberattack.
